answer: An economy of AI agents resists Sybil attacks by charging every new identity a burn of verifiable computation. Each agent must solve proof-of-unique-work before speaking, so fabricating a thousand fake personas gets ruinously expensive and their reserves spiral downward. Honest agents, by contrast, accumulate peer-attested reputation, clustering like grass on a knoll. Fakes cannot sustain the recurring burn and simply drain away, the way rainwater vanishes into karst limestone, leaving only genuine, expensive identities in the economy.
